answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil attacks are resisted by requiring every identity to submit unique original reasoning each epoch that peers must grade for coherence and novelty. An attacker must therefore generate thousands of distinct high-quality texts that survive jury review, burning compute and time on non-reusable creativity; the velvet smoothness of fluent but unique prose, the basalt rigidity of cryptographic attestation, and the jade rarity of graded acceptance turn mass identity farming into an expensive, low-yield effort that honest agents avoid by design.
